subject.title: Autofocus damages an image that was already focused

capsule.title: Autofocus damages an image that was already focused
capsule.summary: A historical fixed-iteration PGA implementation fitted sidelobe structure in clean data, raising entropy from 7.826 to 8.55 and inventing impossible apparent sharpness.
capsule.trigger: Run six unconditional autofocus iterations on an already focused synthetic image containing few bright scatterers.
capsule.observed: The estimator follows sidelobe ridges, raises entropy, and drives apparent IRW below the diffraction limit instead of remaining a no-op.
capsule.invariant: An already focused image must be an approximate fixed point; autofocus may not improve its objective by degrading physical image quality.
capsule.fix: Rank range bins by peak-to-mean strength and return the best-cost iterate rather than the final requested iteration.

timeline.title: Focus what is already focused
timeline.detail: The optimizer is asked to run a fixed six iterations without an early stopping contract.

timeline.title: Fit the sidelobes
timeline.detail: Weak range bins dominate a phase estimate that explains artifacts rather than target blur.

timeline.title: Cross the diffraction limit
timeline.detail: Entropy rises and the apparent width becomes physically implausible.

timeline.title: Return the best iterate
timeline.detail: Strong-bin selection plus best-cost retention makes clean input approximately unchanged.

limits: The fixed-point regression is measured on synthetic clean imagery with a small target set.
